memory_candidates.content: A test fixture that needs an authentic (unstubbed) exercise of git-commit-scoped.sh's V13 gitignore-path gate must copy scripts/lib/specs-ignore-lib.sh into the sandbox's .claude/scripts/lib/ directory. Without it, specs_ignore_lib_available stays empty inside the real script (guarded `source ... 2>/dev/null` silently fails) and the script falls through to an unrelated downstream check (V7's staged-but-unindexed mismatch, exit 2) instead of V13's dedicated exit 8/9. Several existing fixture builders in this codebase already know this (test-git-commit-scoped.sh's own REQUIRED_SCRIPTS array), but a sibling suite's setup_sandbox can still be missing it even when it otherwise copies git-commit-scoped.sh itself.

When a phase's own declared verification bullet surfaces a FAIL that traces to a file outside the plan's Files to modify / the task's declared file_scope, confirm it is genuinely pre-existing by running the specific failing check directly against the live, unmodified file (not by git-stashing a multi-file uncommitted change set in a shared working tree, which risks losing or scrambling concurrent work). Record the confirmed-pre-existing finding as a non-blocking issues.jsonl entry, add a #### Reasoned Exclusions record to the plan citing that entry as evidence, and close the phase [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] rather than either silently claiming a clean pass or parking the phase at [PARTIAL].

sapience_notes.subject: git-commit-scoped.sh V13 gate and git check-ignore
sapience_notes.value: git check-ignore -q correctly reports a directory pathspec (with or without a trailing slash) and a file pathspec nested under an ignored parent directory as ignored, matching a root-level .gitignore entry like `specs/`. The gate's correctness was never the issue in this task; the only failure mode found was a test fixture that forgot to copy the predicate library (specs-ignore-lib.sh) into its sandbox.

sapience_notes.subject: git add's partial-failure behavior on a mixed ignored/non-ignored pathspec list
sapience_notes.value: git add -- <ignored-path> <non-ignored-path> exits nonzero (1) and prints an ignored-paths warning, but still stages the non-ignored path(s) in that same invocation. A caller chaining `git add ... && git commit` will therefore skip the commit entirely once any one of several directory pathspecs becomes gitignored, even though some of the other paths would otherwise have staged successfully.

sapience_notes.subject: git-commit-scoped.sh's --honest-index-rows addendum
sapience_notes.value: The addendum's Python helper (orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's call site) loads HEAD:specs/state.json and the staged :specs/state.json via `git show`; either call raising an exception (an absent git history, or a path never committed) is caught and the helper exits silently before printing anything, suppressing the addendum rather than erroring. This was the correct, already-implemented behavior confirmed during this task, requiring no code change.

sapience_notes.subject: Decision: V13 skip dedup key excludes dispatch_seq
sapience_notes.value: Decided to key the V13 skip-recording dedup identity on session_id + the V13 marker + exit code, deliberately excluding dispatch_seq, so a wholly-ignored-specs repository that completes across multiple /orchestrate cycles within one session still gets exactly one issues.jsonl/events.jsonl entry rather than one per cycle. A session-scoped identity is the correct abstraction level for a per-invocation cap.

sapience_notes.subject: check-record-versioning.sh and check-task-references.sh REPO_ROOT/PATH_SCOPE invocation from a source-store subtree
sapience_notes.value: Both scripts must be invoked with REPO_ROOT set to the actual project root (never the source-store extension directory itself) and PATH_SCOPE given as the repo-root-relative path into the source store (e.g. agent-system/extensions/core/context/standards), or the script either reports the scope as not existing or fails to locate its own shared pattern library.
